title: Agent Archivist upload attestation (attestation_version 1)
description: The durable uploader-and-request provenance record binding one frozen upload to the occurrence it delivered (plan Sections 7.1, 7.4, and 7.5; STO-004, STO-013; SID-006). The server writes it as RFC 8785 canonical JSON at the deterministic attestation key after the bound occurrence manifest is durable. Identity is deliberately separate from the occurrence: attestation_id folds in the uploader and the frozen request, so an origin and an authorized relay uploading the same source event converge on one occurrence while recording distinct, separately auditable attestations (EC-05A), and retries of one frozen request converge on the very same attestation object (STO-004). The record binds who presented what frozen request for which occurrence; it never duplicates transcript content, and per-attempt material — authorization epoch, key, and timestamp, the per-attempt signature, and the server commit time — exists only in the signed receipt (plan Section 7.5). Unknown optional fields are retained and their semantics ignored (plan Section 7.1); the reserved names below are rejected outright because per-attempt or server material frozen here would make byte-identical retries impossible.

x-archivist.writeOrder: after the bound occurrence manifest is durable (plan Section 7.5; RCPT-001: a request succeeds only once blob, occurrence, and attestation are all durable)
x-archivist.identityStability: STO-013: retries of one frozen request converge to one attestation; a distinct authorized uploader or request remains separately auditable — never an overwrite of the occurrence or of another attestation
x-archivist.consistency: delegation=direct requires uploader_client_id == origin_client_id; delegation=relay requires them to differ and the uploader to hold verified origin/uploader delegation (plan Section 5, server flow step; ID-005). This cross-field relation and agreement with the bound occurrence manifest are server-side validation (VAL-002), not schema syntax.

delegation-relation.description: Relation of the uploader to the origin for the frozen request this attestation records (plan Section 7.5; STO-013): `direct` — the uploader is the origin client; `relay` — an authorized uploader presents the origin's frozen occurrence on its behalf (ID-005: a relay never replaces origin identity with its own). Server-derived from the verified authorization and consistent with the two client fields. Security-bearing: an unknown value fails closed.

attestation_version.description: Upload-attestation schema major version (plan Section 7.1 version axis `attestation_version`). Integer, currently 1; readers retain old-version support. New optional fields land inside v1; new required fields, redefined fields, or changed identity rules require v2.

attestation_id.description: The record's own deterministic identity (plan Section 7.4; STO-013): H("attestation-v1", occurrence_id, uploader_client_id, request_id), constructed per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json and re-derivable from this record's own fields. Retries of one frozen request reproduce it exactly, so a lost-response retry rewrites the identical object (STO-004); a distinct uploader or a re-frozen request yields a distinct identity and a second, coexisting record (EC-05A).

tenant_id.description: Issuer-created tenant identifier (plan Section 7.4). Must equal the tenant of the bound occurrence; server-side validation (VAL-002).

occurrence_id.description: The occurrence this attestation delivered (STO-013 binds it). Many attestations may name one occurrence — one per distinct (uploader, request) pair — and none of them modifies it: uploader fields never touch occurrence identity (plan Section 3; EC-05A).

origin_client_id.description: The origin recorded on the bound occurrence, repeated here (STO-013) so the delegation relation is auditable from this object alone. Under `relay` this is the origin's identity, not the uploader's (ID-005; SID-006: original provenance preserved, uploader provenance recorded independently).

uploader_client_id.description: The installation that presented the frozen request (plan Sections 7.4 and 7.5). Equals `origin_client_id` under `direct`; an authorized delegate under `relay`. An identity-hash input of `attestation_id`, so a relay upload can never collide with, or overwrite, the origin's own attestation.

request_id.description: The frozen upload request identifier (plan Sections 7.3 and 7.4; STO-013): a UUIDv7 generated when the spool entry was created and reused across every retry of that request, so retries converge on the same attestation. A re-frozen request (for example after the spool entry was lost) carries a fresh UUIDv7 and stays separately auditable. An identity-hash input of `attestation_id` and the receipt's correlation handle, never a security identity.

delegation.description: Direct-versus-relay relation of this upload (plan Section 7.5; STO-013). Durably recorded rather than inferred, so relay audit history survives without re-deriving authorization state; a relay attestation coexists with the origin's own and with the single source occurrence (EC-05A).

capture_time.description: UTC time the uploader captured (discovered and spooled) the chunk (plan Section 7.3; STO-013 capture timestamp). Uploader-asserted (PI-07) and frozen per request: retries reuse it, a re-frozen request records its own later capture time — which is why this field is attestation material, not part of the source-stable occurrence.

envelope_creation_time.description: UTC time the uploader froze the envelope that this request presented (plan Section 7.3; STO-013 envelope timestamp). Frozen with the spool entry; retries reuse the same value, and per-attempt authorization timestamps stay outside this record entirely.
